subject: Residency certification & deletion processes — Marketplace partner Q&A
messages:
From: Liora Kaplan <lk@enterpriseone.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@cloudmarketplace.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing — residency/retention questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the intro yesterday. Before we finalize the marketplace listing and legal review, our security and procurement teams asked for a short Q&A on three specific items around data residency and deletion across the three cloud marketplaces (AWS, GCP, Azure):

1) Where customer-owned inputs and logs are stored by default for each marketplace region — do you pin to a single provider per marketplace region or is it multi-cloud?
2) Retention defaults and how customers can request shorter retention or opt out of telemetry (audit/logs/usage).
3) Deletion certification — can Redwood provide a deletion attestation (DocuSign) and what is the timeline to purge cached/kv data for a tenant after contract termination?

We need this summary by EOD PT on Tuesday so our Marketplace ops can complete the onboarding checklist. Short bullets are fine — we just need to confirm we won't block the listing.

Appreciate it,
Liora
Senior Cloud Security Manager
EnterpriseOne

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liora Kaplan <lk@enterpriseone.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency/retention questions

Hi Liora — thanks, happy to summarize. High level answers below; attaching our deletion playbook and a mapping sheet that shows default storage tiers per cloud/region. Vanessa, Sergio — please chime in if I miss any nuance.

1) Storage by marketplace region:
- Hosted Marketplace (Redwood-hosted endpoints): default storage location is determined by Marketplace region selection. For AWS marketplace regions we pin to the AWS region chosen (single-provider). For GCP listings, objects and logs are placed in the GCP region. For Azure marketplace, we pin to the Azure region. We do not cross-replicate customer input data across clouds by default. See attachment: residency-mapping-azure-gcp-aws.xlsx

2) Retention defaults & opt-outs:
- Telemetry (token-level logs, system metrics): default retention 90 days; customers can request 30/60/90-day policies via contract addendum for Marketplace listings.
- KV/prefix caches: short-lived by default (48–72 hours) and can be configured with tenant-level TTLs; permanent storage of customer data requires explicit opt-in (e.g., dataset uploads).
- Opt-out: Marketplace customers can opt out of product-usage telemetry when they purchase through a private listing; we provide a toggle and a Data Processing Amendment.

3) Deletion attestation & purge timeline:
- We provide a DocuSign-ready deletion attestation for Marketplace partners. Standard timeline: logical deletion within 24 hours, physical purge from active serving layers within 7 days, and removal from backups/archives on the next snapshot cycle (up to 90 days depending on the backup retention policy). We can shorten the backup purge window for enterprise deals in contract.

Next steps: if that matches your needs I can circulate the signed attestation template (DocuSign link) and Vanessa can confirm the Azure/GCP nuance on backups.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-deletion-playbook_v2.pdf (summary + checklist)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Liora Kaplan <lk@enterpriseone.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency/retention questions

Liora — quick clarifications from an infra/ops perspective:

- AWS: when a marketplace listing is created for us-east-1, all active objects and logs live in S3 & CloudWatch in us-east-1. Backups are snapshot-based and retained per the account-level snapshot policy; default backup retention is 90 days.
- GCP: we use regional GCS buckets and Stackdriver logging pinned to the selected region. GCP's nearline/archival copies may be in a different physical zone in the same geographical region; we do not intentionally replicate to a different cloud provider.
- Azure: Blob storage + Log Analytics in the selected region. Note that certain Azure marketplace integrations require a small management plane component that may call global endpoints for telemetry — we can limit that and document it in the attestation if required.

Deletion mechanics (technical):
- Logical delete: we mark tenant data as deleted in meta-store and revoke access immediately (within minutes).
- Serving layer purge: caches and KV cleared on the next GC window — typically 48–72 hours.
- Archive purge: snapshots and cold archives are marked for deletion and pruned on a scheduled job (configurable, default 90 days). For Marketplace deals we can offer a 30-day archive purge if requested and contracted.

I'll update the residency mapping spreadsheet to call out the management-plane telemetry endpoints and add a column for "contract-eligible purge window". Sending revised sheet now.

—Vanessa
Head of Cloud Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency-mapping-azure-gcp-aws.xlsx

1) Can you route me the DocuSign attestation so our legal can review and sign? We prefer a clause that shortens archive purge to 30 days for the listing.
2) Can Redwood confirm whether the management-plane telemetry callouts for Azure can be disabled or routed to EU-only endpoints for customers in Europe? We have customers who will only accept EU-bound management telemetry.

If you can send the DocuSign link and a one-line confirmation on Azure management-plane routing by EOD PT today, we can greenlight the listing.

Best,
Liora
